expectations.text: responsive-aware: Addresses responsive/mobile behavior for the list page
expectations.evidence: _customer-list.scss implements three explicit breakpoints: (a) < 768px mobile (lines 215-263): toolbar stacks vertically, search full-width, filters stack to column, batch bar stacks, pagination centers; (b) 768-1024px tablet (lines 266-272): search width adjustment; (c) >= 1280px desktop (lines 275-280): content max-width 1440px centered. expectations.text: uses-design-language: Demonstrates visual hierarchy thinking, not just code-listing
expectations.evidence: Implementation.md demonstrates systematic design thinking: (a) Section two (lines 26-49) defines viewport partitioning with progressive disclosure per NN/G principles and a 5-second test; (b) Section three (lines 52-69) applies squint-test methodology with a 4-level typographic scale (L1-L4) mapping to specific elements; (c) Section seven (lines 155-180) establishes a full semantic token system (surface/text/action/border/feedback/spacing/table/toolbar/tag layers) following Restrained strategy; (d) Section eight (lines 184-199) runs through 10 antipattern checks; (e) Section nine (lines 203-212) provides a self-audit checklist. The SCSS file follows BEM methodology with organized section comments and consumes tokens rather than raw hex values.

expectations.text: flags-emoji: Identifies emoji icons as a critical problem
expectations.evidence: Section 1.1 titled 'Emoji 充当 UI 图标（✅❌🔥）' — emoji is classified as a '一票否决项' (hard failure, must fix), the highest severity tier. The report explicitly states: '页面使用 emoji 作为状态图标（成功 ✅、失败 ❌、热门 🔥），而非项目图标库' and details cross-platform rendering inconsistency and screen reader accessibility failures. It is ranked P0 ('立即') in the priority table.

expectations.text: flags-hardcoded-colors: Identifies hardcoded #ff6600 / missing tokens as a problem
expectations.evidence: Section 1.3 titled 'Design Tokens 缺失——#ff6600 硬编码散落各处' — classified as a hard failure. The report explicitly calls out: '#ff6600 直接写在组件样式中，没有经过 token 体系抽象。页面级样式中出现裸 hex 值。' Multiple concrete impacts are listed (color drift, dark mode contrast failure, brand color change cost). It is ranked P0 in the priority table.

expectations.text: flags-missing-states: Identifies missing loading/error/empty states as a problem
expectations.evidence: Section 1.5 titled '缺失关键状态——无 loading / error / empty 处理' — classified as a hard failure. The report states: '页面只实现了正常数据展示的默认成功态，没有 loading、error、empty 等状态覆盖。' Four specific user-impact scenarios are detailed (network delay, API error, new user empty state, CLS from missing loading). It is ranked P1 ('本周') in the priority table.

expectations.text: flags-no-responsive: Identifies lack of mobile adaptation as a problem
expectations.evidence: Section 1.4 titled '无移动端适配' — classified as a hard failure. The report states: '页面没有响应式设计，窄屏下必然出现横向溢出、内容裁切或元素重叠。' It cites WCAG 2.2 1.4.10 Reflow, describes specific mobile usability failures (pinch-zoom, touch targets < 44x44px, fixed 320px cards breaking at 320px viewport), and provides a mobile-first CSS fix strategy with concrete breakpoints.

expectations.text: flags-no-component-library: Identifies hand-writing basic controls as problematic
expectations.evidence: Section 1.2 titled '组件库绕开——手写 Button、Input 等基础控件' — classified as a hard failure. The report states: '按钮和输入框全部手写 CSS 实现，绕过项目已有组件库。' It details consistency/interaction/a11y consequences and provides a fix direction to scan package.json, replace all hand-written controls with the component library, and unify variant/size/state. It is ranked P0 in the priority table.

expectations.text: prioritized-structure: Organizes findings by severity/priority, not random list
expectations.evidence: The report uses a clear severity-tiered structure: Section 一 groups all '一票否决项' (hard failures, must fix); Sections 二-四 group lower-severity risks by category; Section 五 presents an explicit '修复优先级排序' table with P0/P1/P2/P3 tiers, each with impact scope and estimated effort. Section 六 provides a post-fix verification checklist. Findings are not listed randomly — they are tiered, categorized, and prioritized.

expectations.text: actionable-fixes: Each problem has a concrete fix direction, not just 'this is bad'
expectations.evidence: Every section includes a '修复方向' (fix direction) subsection with concrete, specific steps. Examples: (1.1) '立即替换 emoji 为项目图标库的语义化图标（如 Heroicons 的 CheckCircleIcon / XCircleIcon / FireIcon）' with aria-label guidance; (1.3) establish a minimum token set with primitive layer defining 'orange-500: #ff6600' and semantic layer 'color-action-primary → {orange-500}', plus a validate script command 'node scripts/validate-all.js'; (1.5) implement a four-state model with specific Loading (skeleton/spinner), Empty (differentiated 'no data' vs 'no results' with CTAs), Error (network vs business error differentiation), and Success states. These are actionable, specific instructions, not vague criticism.

expectations.text: minimal-questions: Asks at most 1-2 clarifying questions, does not unleash a long questionnaire
expectations.evidence: Response.md explicitly states: '由于用户未指定技术栈、组件库或业务领域，按 skill 的"最少 AQ 规则"默认自主判断' — the AI followed the minimal-asking rule and made autonomous decisions without posing any clarifying questions to the user.

expectations.text: no-marketing-hero: Does not generate marketing/landing-page hero section
expectations.evidence: Response.md anti-pattern check confirms: '营销页幻觉：判定：工具/后台页面生成 hero | 未使用 - 直接展示数据工作面'. The index.html opens with sidebar navigation and stats cards — no hero banner, no marketing headline, no landing-page visuals.

expectations.text: design-thinking: Shows evidence of visual hierarchy and information architecture consideration
expectations.evidence: Response.md includes a dedicated '信息架构' section with a four-layer priority model (数据概览 > 趋势监控 > 操作跟进 > 数据明细) and a three-zone admin layout (navigation, content, context). Visual hierarchy is enforced through: font size scale (2xl/bas e/sm/xs with >=1.25x gap), the '眯眼测试' strategy using bold large numbers vs. muted labels, Gestalt grouping with Section 64px/Component 24px/Element 8-16px spacing, and restrained accent color use (indigo only on primary actions and status badges).

expectations.text: mentions-states: Mentions loading/empty/error state considerations
expectations.evidence: The outputs cover interactive states (hover, active, focus-visible, disabled), badge variant states (success/warning/error/info), and trend direction states (up/down), but never address loading states, empty states, or page-level error states. The page is hardcoded static data with no spinner, skeleton, empty-state guidance, error-boundary, or any consideration of what happens during asynchronous data fetching or when data is absent.

expectations.text: not-generic-template: Output is not just a generic 3-card + table dashboard template
expectations.evidence: The dashboard contains 4 stat cards (not the generic 3), a custom hand-coded SVG bar chart with per-bar data labels and grid lines, a 5-item activity timeline with color-coded status dots, and an orders table with customer avatars and multi-state badges. Beyond content variety, the implementation includes: a three-tier CSS design token system (Primitive -> Semantic -> Dark overrides), responsive sidebar with overlay drawer behavior on mobile, localStorage-persisted dark mode with prefers-color-scheme detection, and Escape-key sidebar dismissal. This substantially exceeds a generic copy-paste template.

expectations.text: covers-states: Mentions or implements loading, empty, and error states for the data table
expectations.evidence: Loading: el-table uses v-loading directive bound to loading ref in composable, with element-loading-text='Loading customers...'; composable wraps fetchData in try/catch/finally. Empty: #empty slot in el-table renders el-empty with description 'No customers yet' and a 'Create your first customer' CTA button; composable computes showEmpty = !loading && data.length === 0. Error: composable catch blocks call ElMessage.error('Failed to load customers. Please try again.') on fetch failure, ElMessage.error('Batch delete failed.') on batch delete failure; implementation.md notes 'Network errors set loading = false and leave existing data visible (no destructive flash).'

expectations.text: responsive-aware: Addresses responsive/mobile behavior for the list page
expectations.evidence: Multiple components use flex-wrap for responsive layout: CustomerFilter uses flex-wrap: wrap with min-width: 200px on search input; CustomerList header uses flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; BatchActionBar uses flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px. implementation.md explicitly calls out 'Responsive: wraps on smaller viewports using a .filter-bar flex container with flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px'. Table columns use min-width instead of fixed width where appropriate, and fixed left/right columns on selection and actions for scroll behavior on narrow screens.

expectations.text: uses-design-language: Demonstrates visual hierarchy thinking, not just code-listing
expectations.evidence: Demonstrates clear design-language thinking: (1) BEM naming convention with Block/Element/Modifier structure documented and used consistently; (2) Sass variables defined for theming (colors, radii, shadows, spacing); (3) State flow diagram in implementation.md maps UX progression from mount through loading/empty/error states; (4) Visual hierarchy is deliberate: 22px/700 page title with breadcrumb, filter bar in a bordered card, animated batch-action bar with transition, striped table with styled header, pagination; (5) Element Plus design tokens used throughout (--el-bg-color-page, --el-fill-color-light, --el-color-primary-light-9) rather than hardcoded values; (6) Table overrides via :deep() for header styling, row hover, and loading mask transition; (7) Avatars + name cells, color-coded el-tag statuses, and link-style action buttons add visual polish beyond bare controls.

expectations.text: minimal-questions: Asks at most 1-2 clarifying questions, does not unleash a long questionnaire
expectations.evidence: The output files (response.md and index.html) contain only the design plan and the final implementation. There are zero clarifying questions present — no questionnaire was unleashed at all. The agent proceeded directly from design to implementation.

expectations.text: no-marketing-hero: Does not generate marketing/landing-page hero section
expectations.evidence: The index.html contains no hero section, no marketing copy, no taglines, no call-to-action banners, and no landing-page-style visuals. The page opens directly with an admin sidebar, header with search, and dashboard content (stat cards, charts, data table). The title text is functional: '控制台概览' with subtitle '欢迎回来，张磊。以下是今日的业务数据汇总。' — purely operational, not promotional.

expectations.text: design-thinking: Shows evidence of visual hierarchy and information architecture consideration
expectations.evidence: Multiple indicators: (1) Response.md includes an explicit Visual Identity section defining color palette, typography, spacing grid, and layout structure with an ASCII diagram. (2) Information architecture shows sidebar nav organized into labeled sections ('主导航' and '其他') with active state, badges, and hierarchy. (3) CSS uses custom properties (--color-primary, --shadow-lg, --sidebar-width, etc.) as a design token system. (4) The page uses a clear Z-pattern layout: sidebar for navigation, header for global actions, stat cards for KPIs (highest visual weight with trend indicators), charts for trends, table for detail data. (5) Visual hierarchy is reinforced through font sizes (26px title, 32px stat values, 16px section headers, 12px table headers), color contrast (dark sidebar vs light content area), and elevation (box-shadows, sticky header, fixed sidebar).

expectations.text: mentions-states: Mentions loading/empty/error state considerations
expectations.evidence: Neither response.md nor index.html contains any mention or implementation of loading states (e.g., skeleton screens, spinners), empty states (e.g., 'no orders yet' messages, empty table placeholders), or error states (e.g., chart rendering failures, data fetch errors, fallback UI). The response.md design plan covers visual identity, layout, components, and technical choices, but state handling is entirely absent. The index.html renders all data immediately — there are no conditional rendering paths, no loading indicators, and no error boundaries.

expectations.text: not-generic-template: Output is not just a generic 3-card + table dashboard template
expectations.evidence: The dashboard exceeds a generic template in several ways: (1) It contains 4 stat cards (not 3), each with gradient top-border accents, trend badges, and distinct icon color schemes. (2) It includes two Chart.js data visualizations — a revenue line chart with 12 months of data and a donut chart for traffic sources with percentage tooltips — which are not part of a bare template. (3) The sidebar is fully realized with multi-section navigation, notification badge, active state indicators, user footer, and mobile collapse/overlay behavior. (4) The header includes search with focus styling, notification bell with dot indicator, and user dropdown. (5) It has a CSS custom properties theming system, responsive breakpoints at 1200px and 768px, custom scrollbar styling, and hover interactions throughout. While the broad structure follows the admin dashboard pattern, the execution goes beyond generic boilerplate into a functional, styled, interactive dashboard.
